restrictions: Complete fixed-IV SHA-256, steps 0 through 31, standard expansion, feed-forward, FIPS 180-4 padding and all 256 digest bits. Every message is 55 bytes: W0..W12 are the group prefix, W13 = (y<<8)|0x80, W14 = 0, W15 = 440.

Generic grouped birthday search extended from jaazinn 6b88bdb7 and winglock 68ca8e4f, both unpromoted and credited as co-authors: 2^104 groups from two fresh uniform words, y = 0..2^24-1, N = 2^128. New here: four messages share each body instruction in one 256-bit word (proof Section 3). The 160-bit key (A28, A29, E28, E29, D30) with D30 = A30 - E30 = T2_30 - A26 is a fixed function of the digest. Each key match is verified with two whole reference compressions. At most 2^110 verifications.

Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM, 64 registers, collision-frontier-v5, C = 2224. One 256-bit add, subtract, AND, OR, XOR, NOT, shift, compare, branch, load, store or random word costs 1/2224. A packed instruction is one primitive. Sigma/sigma are the doubling formulas plus an M4 mask, 8 operations. Per batch of 4: 563 counted body operations, 71 extract-and-pack, 52 table, 3 loop, total 689, which is 172.25 per message. Charged 196 per message.

Group setup is under 1000 operations and is charged 1 unit per group. Each verification is 3 units. T <= 2^128*196/2224 + 2^104 + 3*2^110 + 1 < 2^124.5, so the claimed time_log2 is 124.60. This cap holds on every run. Only the success probability uses heuristic H1. A reconstruction of 210 operations per message is still under 124.60.

No differential weakness, full-scale execution or stored collision is claimed, and no improvement over the nominal reference identifier is asserted. The declared experiments are 20-bit masked analogues. They check lane agreement with a plain compression; they are not an attack-cost measurement.

heuristics.statement: For the 2^128 messages of the algorithm (independent uniform 416-bit prefixes, y = 0..2^24-1), the failure events F1 (no full-digest collision), F2 (every colliding pair has its earlier member overwritten in the 140-bit index slot) and F4 (more than 2^110 key matches) have probabilities at most the independent-uniform-digest values: Pr[F1] < 0.6065307, Pr[F2] < 4.07e-5, Pr[F4] <= 2^-15, so success > 0.39339. The 160-bit key and its top 140 bits are uniform images of a uniform digest.
heuristics.scope: Used only for the success probability (proof Section 7). Output correctness, the worst-case time cap, memory, lane isolation and the operation count do not depend on H1. Within-group pairs are a 2^-104 fraction of all pairs. Multiplying N by 1.0108 adds 0.0155 to log2 T and lifts model success to about 0.3998. Two independent runs repair a shortfall below 0.39 at a cost of at most 1.0 in log2 T.
heuristics.extrapolation: Evidence is two organizer-executed scaled analogues on the real target, N_t = 2^10 messages and 20-bit masks, in the same N_t^2/2^w = 1 regime as N^2/2^256 = 1, compared with the random-model values 0.3926 and 0.3918. The claim applies that model to the full 256-bit digest and 2^128 messages, an extrapolation of more than 220 bits. It is the standard random-function premise of a generic 256-bit collision bound, also used by the grouped packages this one extends.
heuristics.limitations: H1 is not proved. Masked experiments cannot detect structure that appears only at full width or at 2^128 messages, and the organizer seeds are public. With 256 trials each experiment resolves success only to about +-0.03. Observations are participant-reported; the organizer independently checks returned pairs against the real digest. The 0.0034 allowance between 0.39339 and 0.39 is a judgement. Lane isolation is not part of H1: it is a bit-position argument, and a mismatched lane in the organizer check would be a concrete counterexample to the program, not to H1.
